// Context & Vision

About Smart India Hackathon 2026

Empowering DSMNRU Innovators

Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is a nationwide initiative by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell (MIC) and AICTE to engage students in solving real-world problems faced by central & state ministries, PSUs, and private industries.

At Institute of Engineering & Technology (IET), DSMNRU Lucknow, the internal hackathon round acts as an incubator where student teams present their hardware or software solutions, receive live expert feedback, and secure the university’s official nomination for SIH 2026.

Mission Statement

To cultivate a culture of innovation, product design, and problem-solving among engineering and general discipline students at Dr. Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University.

Nationwide Initiative

Smart India Hackathon is a flagship initiative by MoE’s Innovation Cell & AICTE to solve pressing challenges of ministries, industries, and NGOs.

Internal Screening

DSMNRU internal round serves as the gateway to evaluate, filter, and refine student ideas before official submission to the national portal.

Faculty Mentorship

Top internal teams get dedicated guidance from IET faculty members and industry experts to polish prototypes and pitches.

National Grand Finale

Nominated teams compete against top institutions across India for cash prizes up to ₹1,00,000 per problem statement at national nodal centers.

// Guidelines & Compliance

Rules & Regulations (13 Mandatory Rules)

Strictly enforced rules to ensure fair play, academic integrity, and seamless SIH portal nomination.

Rule #01Critical Rule

Mandatory Team Size of Exactly 6 Members

Each team MUST consist of exactly 6 regular students from DSMNRU. Neither fewer nor more than 6 members are allowed in a team.

Group: Team & Eligibility
Rule #02Gender Rule

Mandatory Female Diversity Rule

Every team MUST include at least one female team member. All-male teams are strictly disqualified per official SIH guidelines.

Group: Team & Eligibility
Rule #03Strict Enforcement

One Student = One Team Only

A student can belong to AT MOST ONE team across the entire university. Dual registrations are strictly prohibited and enforced via database unique constraints.

Group: Team & Eligibility
Rule #04Eligibility

Institutional Eligibility (DSMNRU Regular Students)

All team members must be enrolled in regular UG, PG, or PhD programs at Dr. Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University, Lucknow.

Group: Team & Eligibility
Rule #05Mentor Rule

Faculty Mentors Provision (1-2 Mentors)

Teams may have 1 to 2 faculty mentors. Mentors provide guidance only and DO NOT count towards the 6 student members.

Group: Team & Eligibility
Rule #06Problem Domain

Original Problem Statement Alignment

Solutions must directly map to one of the published problem statements (or open innovation domain) approved by the internal hackathon committee.

Group: Submission & Building
Rule #07AI Policy

Use of AI Tools & Generative AI Policy

AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot) are allowed for ideation and code reference, BUT teams MUST defend all code, architecture, and design live.

Group: Submission & Building
Rule #08Deliverable

Repository & Live Demo Requirement

Every software team must maintain a public Git repository with regular commits. Hardware teams must present a physical operational model.

Group: Submission & Building
Rule #09Format Rule

PPT Presentation Format Compliance

Idea synopses must adhere strictly to the official 5-slide SIH PPT format (Problem, Proposed Solution, Tech Stack, Feasibility, Impact).

Group: Submission & Building
Rule #10Disqualification

Zero Tolerance for Plagiarism & Pre-built Projects

Submitting pre-existing commercial projects or copy-pasting existing open-source projects without significant original work results in immediate disqualification.

Group: Judging & Conduct
Rule #11Evaluation

Live Q&A Defense Before Jury

All 6 team members must be present during evaluation. Jury members reserve the right to question any member on specific code logic or hardware design.

Group: Judging & Conduct
Rule #12Conduct

Code of Conduct & Academic Integrity

Participants must maintain professional decorum, respect fellow competitors, and abide by DSMNRU university campus discipline guidelines.

Group: Judging & Conduct
Rule #13Final Authority

Finality of Jury & SPOC Decisions

The decision of the internal jury panel and SPOC Ms. Shalini Raghuvanshi regarding team selection and SIH nomination is final and binding.

Group: Judging & Conduct
// Jury Scoring Rubric

Evaluation Criteria & Weightage

Transparent metrics used by the internal screening panel to evaluate and shortlist winning teams.

25%

Innovation & Originality

Uniqueness of the proposed solution, novelty of the approach, and creative application of technology to solve the problem statement.

Metric #1Internal Jury Rubric
25%

Technical Feasibility & Architecture

Robustness of technology stack, code quality, clean software/hardware architecture, and realistic implementation viability.

Metric #2Internal Jury Rubric
20%

Usability, UX & Accessibility

User-friendly interface design, smooth workflow, responsive layout, and inclusivity for differently-abled users.

Metric #3Internal Jury Rubric
15%

Scalability & Real-World Impact

Potential for real-world deployment, scalability to handle large user bases or geographic regions, and societal/economic value.

Metric #4Internal Jury Rubric
15%

Presentation & Live Q&A Defense

Clarity of presentation pitch, confidence during jury questions, and ability of all 6 team members to defend their implementation.

Metric #5Internal Jury Rubric
